Asset type: one original-size-compatible Hearts of Iron IV character portrait replacement.
Image 1 is the original HOI4 portrait and composition target. Image 2 is the user's exact 奶龙 identity reference: a smooth golden-yellow round creature with green rings around black eyes, a small horizontal mouth and creamy belly.
Replace the human head, body and exposed human skin with this recognizable yellow mascot. RETAIN the original person's visible hairstyle, hairline, hair color and eyebrows as distinguishing features attached to the mascot, adapting them to its round head. Preserve the original garment design, uniform type, fabric, colors, headgear, glasses, decorations, accessories, expression, gaze, pose, action, framing, lighting, background and painterly color treatment. Keep all existing garment design details and insignia; do not invent new hats, uniforms, medals or symbols. Keep the yellow creature's anatomy, large green-ringed black eyes and small horizontal mouth; do not restore human skin, human nose or human ears. Express the original mood through its creature eyes and mouth plus retained eyebrows.
Facial-hair placement: wherever the original has a moustache and chin beard, their top-to-bottom order is eyes, UPPER-LIP moustache, small horizontal mouth, chin beard. Never place the visible mouth above the moustache or turn the moustache into a second beard. Clean-shaven originals stay clean-shaven.
When the source actually has a moustache, show it as a distinct visible band of hair with fine painted hair texture ABOVE the mascot's existing grey lip and small mouth. Retain the visible shape, symbol count and arrangement of source collar patches and existing decorations. Do not invent chest medallions. Any source note markings that are illegible remain indistinct texture; do not invent readable serial numbers, identification codes, words or labels.
Collar and anatomy: use a compact rounded mascot head seated close to broad shoulders, with a very short, wide neck transition. The head silhouette is nearly round or a SHORT egg shape. Its chin rests immediately above the garment collar, without copying the original human neck length. Preserve the shoulder position and crop by broadening the fitted garment; do not fill that space with a tall yellow column.
The garment meets the underside of a visibly rounded chin. There is no separate exposed vertical neck column between the head and collar, including bald and three-quarter-view portraits.
The lower head silhouette curves inward toward its base instead of continuing down as parallel straight yellow sides. Raise and broaden the original collar and shoulders to meet that curved chin; do not insert an extra yellow neck roll underneath it.

Do not turn a closed military collar into a deep V-neck or unbuttoned shirt. Preserve open lapels/shirt collars only where the original is actually open.
